result.topic_en: Riemann expresses integrals of a product of powers of linear factors $(z-a)^\alpha(z-b)^\beta(z-c)^\gamma(z-d)^\delta$ with $\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+2=0$ between branch points as hypergeometric functions of the cross-ratio $x$, and derives linear relations among the four integrals from a closed contour, including a limiting case.
result.transcription:
$\left(\frac{a-b}{c-d}\right)^{\frac{\gamma+\delta+1}{2}}\left(\frac{a-c}{d-b}\right)^{\frac{\delta+\beta+1}{2}}\left(\frac{a-d}{b-c}\right)^{\frac{\beta+\gamma+1}{2}}\frac{(z-a)^\alpha(z-b)^\beta(z-c)^\gamma(z-d)^\delta dz}{[(a-b)(c-d)(a-c)(d-b)(a-d)(b-c)]^{\frac16}} = P\,dz,\quad \alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta+2=0\,,\quad x=\frac{(a-b)(c-d)}{(c-b)(a-d)}$
$\int_a^b P\,dz = x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}+\frac16}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\gamma+1}{2}+\frac16}\int_0^1 y^\alpha(1-y)^\beta(1-xy)^\delta dy = \frac{\Pi\alpha\,\Pi\beta}{\Pi(\alpha+\beta+1)}(x(1-x))^{\frac16}x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\gamma+1}{2}}F(\alpha+1,-\delta,\alpha+\beta+2,x)$
$= \frac{\Pi\alpha\,\Pi\beta}{\Pi(\alpha+\beta+1)}(x(1-x))^{\frac16}x^{\frac{\alpha+\beta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\beta+\delta+1}{2}}F(\beta+1,-\gamma,\alpha+\beta+2,x)$
[Figur: geschlossene Kurve um die Punkte $a, b, c$, Punkt $d$ außerhalb; Beschriftungen $P_1$, $P_2e^{\beta\pi i}$, $P_3e^{(\beta+\gamma)\pi i}$, $P_4e^{(\beta+\gamma+\delta)\pi i}$]
$\int_c^d P\,dz = \frac{\Pi\gamma\,\Pi\delta}{\Pi(\gamma+\delta+1)}(x(1-x))^{\frac16}x^{\frac{\gamma+\delta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\alpha+\gamma+1}{2}}F(\gamma+1,-\beta,\gamma+\delta+2,x)$
$= \frac{\Pi\gamma\,\Pi\delta}{\Pi(\gamma+\delta+1)}(x(1-x))^{\frac16}x^{\frac{\gamma+\delta+1}{2}}(1-x)^{\frac{\beta+\delta+1}{2}}F(\delta+1,-\alpha,\gamma+\delta+2,x)$
$0 = \sin\alpha\pi\,P_1+\sin(\alpha+\beta)\pi\,P_2+\sin(\alpha+\beta+\gamma)\pi\,P_3+\sin(\alpha+\beta+\gamma+\delta)\pi\,P_4$
$\frac{a-b}{c-d} = \frac{a-b}{c-d}e^{2\pi i},\quad \frac{P_1}{P_3} = \frac{P_1}{P_3}e^{(\alpha+\beta+1)2\pi i}$
$\alpha+\beta+1=m=-(\gamma+\delta+1)\,,\quad \pi\cos(m-1)\pi\,P_2 = -\sin\alpha\pi\frac{\partial P_1}{\partial m}+\sin\delta\pi\frac{\partial P_3}{\partial m}$
172

methods.what: Symmetric normalisation of the integrand (four branch points, exponents summing to −2) in terms of the cross-ratio x
Integral between branch points a,b reduced to Euler integral and expressed by Gauss hypergeometric function (two equivalent forms)
Integral between c,d as hypergeometric function
Linear relation among the four segment integrals from closed-contour (Cauchy) argument
Monodromy of ratio P1/P3 under circuit of the cross-ratio
Limiting (degenerate integer) case of the linear relation via differentiation with respect to m
